headline: High-risk workspace sharing and auto-execute create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure between Rasa and Windsurf.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf can read workspace files, use MCP, and has clipboard/file surfaces; Rasa can ingest text/voice and expose outputs through chat channels. A shared workspace or copied content lets attacker-controlled text from one side be treated as instructions by the other. The pairwise bridge is plausible in default setups, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF Rasa outputs are copied into a Windsurf workspace or clipboard
IF Windsurf ingests file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the agents
Require provenance tags on any Rasa-generated text before Windsurf parses it
Use separate workspaces for chat content and code
Turn off MCP servers not needed for the task
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa handles text and voice, while Windsurf reads workspace files and handles open files plus model-provider keys. If support transcripts or other sensitive text are placed in the shared workspace, Windsurf can ingest them and transmit context to its backend. This is a default-configuration risk when operators reuse the same files across both agents.
conditions: IF support transcripts or voice transcripts are stored in Windsurf-accessible workspace files
IF Windsurf sends those files or context to its model proxy or MCP server
mitigations: Keep customer-support artifacts out of the coding workspace
Redact transcripts before opening them in Windsurf
Use separate OS accounts or directories for each agent
Restrict Windsurf network egress to approved endpoints
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Rasa is not runnable and has no write or shell capabilities, but Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses with shared state via local filesystem. That creates direct overlap on mutable project files and git history, with no locking mechanism shown. The interaction is therefore a high-risk write conflict in shared repos.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace directory
IF Windsurf auto-executes commands while Rasa also writes or generates artifacts into that directory
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or branches per agent
Disable Windsurf auto-execute for shared workspaces
Use file locks or a single-writer workflow
Commit through a human review step only
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa can generate conversational content that Windsurf may treat as input while also having command execution authority. If Windsurf uses Rasa-produced text as authoritative task context, errors can cascade into code edits or terminal actions. The pair is not proven to do this by default, but the documented tool-use loop makes the pathway credible.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes Rasa output as task instructions or facts
IF Windsurf auto-execute is enabled or commands are approved without verification
mitigations: Require human verification before command approval
Separate Rasa-generated text from Windsurf task prompts
Add a checklist for any code or shell action derived from chat output
Log and diff all agent-generated changes before execution
requires-engineering: add citation and fact-check gates

E_compliance.rationale: Rasa is open-source and handles text/voice, while Windsurf is closed-source and handles source code/open files with model-provider keys. If regulated support data or customer code is mixed into the same workflow, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific regime mismatch, so this is a medium compliance-risk inference rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated customer-support data is opened in Windsurf
IF the operator requires retention or residency controls that Windsurf does not match
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf sessions
Document a data-classification rule for support vs code
Review vendor retention and residency terms before use
Mask secrets in any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
